label: GO after a2->rare S1 rewarded; larger mid-episode, when belief favours S2
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * np.clip(belief_lo, -4, 4) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (tv("state", -2) == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * np.clip(ep_trial - 10, 0, 40) / 40 ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * np.clip(ep_trial - 70, 0, 20) / 20
explanation: Fires only at GO, and essentially only when the previous trial was a2 -> rare S1 -> rewarded (the trial that tells a model-based agent to switch to a1, unless it believes S2 is good). That indicator alone gives dev R^2 beyond timing 0.36, which is roughly the profile ceiling (all 0.40, all observed 0.38). Within that pattern the magnitude follows a hump over episode time: near zero in the first ~10 trials, rising until about trial 50 and falling again after trial 70. This interaction with episode time is not captured by the per-decile timing baseline and is the largest gain (dev 0.47 -> 0.72). The magnitude is also larger when the ideal-observer belief favours S2 (negative belief_lo, i.e. the rare reward on S1 should be discounted and a2 kept, which matches the earlier stick-with-a2 policy label), when the trial before was rewarded, and when the trial before reached S2. No activity at D1 or D2, and none after any other previous-trial pattern. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.70 (0.65 without the belief term). Observed-only terms reach and exceed the additive ceiling, so dropping the model value/policy appears to cost little here. Misses: windows whose first trial has no visible previous trial cannot be predicted.

issues: Minor: the belief, previous-reward and previous-state effects scale with the episode hump rather than adding to it. Multiplying each one by the hump shape, B*hump*belief_lo etc. (5 terms), raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.70 to 0.78. Weights: hump +0.204, hump*belief_lo -0.057, hump*prev2_rewarded +0.057, hump*prev2_S2 +0.036. So the modulators matter most mid-episode, which the label does not say.

Minor: the fall starts earlier than 'after trial 70'. Per-decile weights for B (test 0.587) are 0.002, 0.003, 0.086 (deciles 2-3), 0.187, 0.238, 0.249, 0.177 (decile 7), 0.023 (deciles 8-9). The peak is at trials 50-69, decile 7 is already lower, and the activation is near zero after 80. The hump claim itself holds: a linear ep_dec interaction gives only 0.34.

The secondary modulators are small. Each adds about 0.005-0.01 test R^2: hump+belief 0.691, +prev2 reward 0.700, +prev2 state 0.697. Their direction is confirmed: belief_lo weight -0.03 (S2-favouring belief raises it), prev2 rewarded +0.04, prev2 S2 +0.03. The belief term is a signed linear effect: |belief_lo| does worse (0.658) and a quadratic term adds nothing. belief_cover adds nothing.

Overclaim: 'past the additive ceiling, so dropping value/policy costs little' compares an interaction model against an additive ceiling (0.40). It does not compare against the earlier value/policy explanation's own interaction score, so the claimed cost of going observed-only is not measured.

The only systematic misses are windows whose first trial has no previous trial (prev = '?'). There the feature fires at about 0.37-0.39 and the fit predicts about 0. This is a limit of the data that the explanation already acknowledges. Phase errors elsewhere are at most 0.004, with no D1/D2 activity and no other previous-trial pattern.
